did_you_know.text: The word “מַחֲזֶה” describes a vision or revelation, not necessarily an ordinary dream. The word “מָגֵן” presents God as a shield protecting Abram.
“The son of my household” need not mean a biological son; it may refer to the person managing the household. Abram therefore fears that his household administrator will become his heir.
The stars serve here as an image of an enormous number that cannot be counted. In the ancient world, the night sky was also important for observing and measuring the seasons.

The phrase “and He counted it to him as righteousness” became central to Jewish and Christian discussions about the relationship between faith and righteousness. Here, “righteousness” means being regarded as right before God.
The expression “to cut a covenant” is probably connected with the cutting of the animals in the ritual described here. This is the origin of the Hebrew phrase for making a binding covenant.

The number 400 is presented as a rounded figure; Exodus 12:40 gives 430 years, so commentators have discussed how to calculate the period of residence and slavery. This shows that biblical numbers are not always calculated in exactly the same way.

The smoking oven and flaming torch passing between the pieces symbolize divine presence. In ancient Near Eastern covenant ceremonies, passing between the cut pieces expressed the seriousness of the commitment.
